title: SF2413 (2019-2020 Regular): Right to carry a firearm without a permit

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2019/0/SF/2413/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Read the introduced bill (no date in file); no vote data. Struck words are minor edits. Section 8 quote joins across a struck 'a permit' (omitted). Section 1(a) declares the Second Amendment guarantees an individual right; that is the bill's own statement, not a duty on a step, so no higher_law_duty.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, new subd. 1c): (b) A person who is not prohibited from possessing a firearm by any law of this state or any federal law shall have the right to carry, hold, or possess a firearm in a motor vehicle, snowmobile, or boat, or on or about the person's clothes or the person, or otherwise in possession or control in a public place.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, new subd. 1d): A person may apply for an optional permit to carry a pistol as provided in this section.
Section 8 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 23): No sheriff, police chief, governmental unit, government official, government employee, or other person or body acting under color of law or governmental authority may change, modify, or supplement these criteria or procedures, or limit the exercise of the right to carry a firearm.
Section 9 (repealer): Minnesota Statutes 2018, sections 624.714, subdivisions 1a, 1b, and 16; and 624.7181, are repealed.
